# Transfer linear-probing evaluation of the 100-epoch ImageNet-1K pretrains

Reproduction of **SPHERE-JEPA (Nicollier et al., 2026), Table 1** — "Frozen-backbone
linear probing accuracy (%) on downstream datasets using ViT-B/14 backbones pretrained
for 100 epochs on ImageNet-1K" — with our backbones instead of the ViT-B/14: a
**D4-equivariant ResNet-50**, a **Hyperbolic ViT-S/8**, and a **plain ViT-S/8** baseline. Auto-generated by
`scripts/make_transfer_results.py` from `logs/eval_transfer_in1k_ep100/per_backbone/`
(14/16 rows complete).

in `src/eval/transfer.py`:

* **Pretraining**: the same ImageNet-1K checkpoints as `Imagenet1K_results.md` (100
  epochs, crop 128, 4 views/image, global batch 256, AdamW, embedding dim 512, no EMA
  teacher — the paper's non-EMA rows). Final checkpoint (epoch 99 = 100 epochs).
* **Frozen backbone features**: the 512-d encoder output *before* the projector,
  deterministic eval transform (resize + centre crop 128, ImageNet normalisation).
* **Downstream datasets** (torchvision, standard splits — train on everything that is
  not the official test split, report on the test split):

  | Dataset | train split | test split | #train | #test | classes |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | DTD (partition 1) | train + val | test | 3,760 | 1,880 | 47 |
  | FGVC-Aircraft (variant) | trainval | test | 6,667 | 3,333 | 100 |
  | CIFAR-10 | train | test | 50,000 | 10,000 | 10 |
  | CIFAR-100 | train | test | 50,000 | 10,000 | 100 |
  | Flowers-102 | train + val | test | 2,040 | 6,149 | 102 |
  | Food-101 | train | test | 75,750 | 25,250 | 101 |
  | Oxford-IIIT Pets | trainval | test | 3,680 | 3,669 | 37 |

* **Linear probe** (same code as the in-domain `Linear (%)` column): one linear layer
  on the standardized frozen features, SGD (momentum 0.9, cosine schedule, 100 epochs,
  batch 256, no weight decay), learning rate chosen on a 10% held-out slice of the
  train split from {0.001, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30}, then refit on the full train
  split; **top-1 accuracy on the test split**. *Avg* is the unweighted mean over the
  seven datasets. No augmentation is used at probe time (features are cached).

## Observations

* **D4-equivariant ResNet-50**: best Avg is LeJEPA + local BallReg (λ0.1, k1→10 dyn) at 54.6 vs 47.8 for LeJEPA/SIGReg (+6.7).
* **Hyperbolic ViT-S/8**: best Avg is LeJEPA + local BallReg (λ0.1, k2) at 64.1 vs 58.0 for LeJEPA/SIGReg (+6.1).
* **Plain ViT-S/8**: best Avg is LeJEPA + local BallReg (λ0.1, k4) at 63.1 vs 56.7 for LeJEPA/SIGReg (+6.4). Every regulariser variant beats SIGReg on DTD, Aircraft, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, Flowers, Food, Pets.
* Hardest datasets for every backbone: Aircraft and Food; easiest: CIFAR10 (the same ordering as the paper's ViT-B/14, where Aircraft is ~10% and CIFAR10 ~82%).
* **Absolute numbers are not comparable to the paper's** (ViT-B/14 at 224 px, 86M params, batch 512): our backbones are ~4x smaller and both pretrained and probed at 128 px, which hurts fine-grained datasets (Aircraft, Pets, Flowers) most. Compare rows *within* a backbone.
